seo.title: Risk Management & Wealth Protection | DNH
seo.description: Identify concentrations, dependencies, liquidity constraints and structural vulnerabilities to clarify wealth-risk priorities.

sections.heading: Risk Management & Wealth Protection: identify hidden vulnerabilities in capital
paragraphs: Risk does not always arrive as a sudden crisis. Asset concentration, limited liquidity or dependence on one income source can make wealth vulnerable to change.
Drawing on Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani’s specialist perspective, DNH helps identify and assess these risks and clarify review priorities.

media.alt: A conceptual view of risk management and wealth protection

sections.heading: Diverse assets do not always mean lower risk
paragraphs: You may hold valuable assets while much of the structure still depends on one market, income source or economic condition.
Understanding those dependencies matters before they turn into financial constraints.

items.title: Capital concentration
items.description: A material share of wealth sits in one asset or market.

items.title: Common risk drivers
items.description: Different assets may respond to the same economic factor.

items.title: Limited liquidity
items.description: Asset values are high, but rapid access to cash is difficult.

items.title: Business dependency
items.description: Personal capital and income depend materially on one business.

items.title: Future financial obligations
items.description: Upcoming payments may not align with available liquid resources.

sections.heading: Risk management means identifying pressure points before a decision
paragraphs: At DNH, risk management does not mean eliminating every risk or predicting a crisis.
It focuses on the wealth structure, its vulnerabilities and the relative importance of different risks.

items.title: Identify risks
items.description: Recognise factors that may affect assets, liquidity or obligations.

items.title: Understand risk relationships
items.description: Identify dependencies that can affect several parts of wealth at once.

items.title: Prioritise vulnerabilities
items.description: Determine which matters deserve greater attention given the circumstances and objectives.

sections.closing: The purpose is a clearer view of wealth risks and the matters that need attention before decisions are made.

sections.heading: Who should consider a wealth-risk review?
sections.intro: As assets, obligations and sources of income become more complex, understanding the connections between risks becomes more important.

items.title: Individuals and investors
items.description: You hold diverse or concentrated assets and want a clearer view of risk, liquidity and financial dependencies.

items.title: Families
items.description: Family wealth involves obligations, future needs and decisions across several people and needs an integrated review.

items.title: Business owners
items.description: Personal wealth or income depends on a business whose performance can affect the wider financial position.

sections.heading: Which part of the wealth structure is more vulnerable?
sections.intro: A risk review is not simply a list of threats. It should show which part of wealth is exposed, how risks connect and which matters require priority attention.

items.title: Concentration and dependency
items.description: Areas dependent on one asset, market or income source.

items.title: Liquidity
items.description: Access to financial resources when they are needed.

items.title: Financial obligations
items.description: Payments and needs that may reduce financial flexibility.

items.title: Environmental risks
items.description: Sensitivity to inflation, currencies, markets and economic developments.

sections.closing: Core question: if economic conditions change, which part of the wealth structure could come under pressure first?
sections.note: Illustrative position: an individual holds much of their wealth in property and a business while facing future obligations. This preview explains the risk-map concept only.

sections.heading: Asset variety does not always create genuine risk diversification
sections.intro: Capital may be divided among several assets while all remain exposed to the same economic change.

items.title: Concentration in one asset
items.description: A material share of wealth depends on changes in one asset’s value.

items.title: Concentration in one market
items.description: Several investments depend on one market or industry.

items.title: Dependence on one income source
items.description: A decline in primary income could affect expenses and obligations.

items.title: Personal and business dependency
items.description: Personal wealth is connected to the financial performance and risks of the business.

sections.closing: The aim is not to remove every concentration, but to understand dependencies and their potential implications.

sections.heading: Capital value matters; access to capital matters too
paragraphs: A valuable asset meets a financial need only if it can be used at the appropriate time.
Liquidity should therefore be considered alongside obligations, inflation, currencies and economic conditions.

items.title: Asset liquidity
items.description: Which assets can become usable cash, when, and at what cost or constraint?

items.title: Future obligations
items.description: Do available resources align with payment timing?

items.title: Inflation and purchasing power
items.description: How could higher prices affect real capital value?

items.title: Currency risk
items.description: How might exchange-rate changes affect assets and financial needs?

items.title: Financing conditions
items.description: What constraints arise if financing costs or access change?

items.title: Economic and external risks
items.description: Which economic, political or international changes may affect the wealth structure?

sections.note: Asset liquidity is distinct from cash already available or access to external financing.

sections.heading: How flexible is the wealth structure if conditions change?
sections.intro: Considering different hypothetical conditions helps identify assets, obligations and income sources that are more sensitive.

items.title: Higher inflation
items.description: Which needs and assets are more exposed if purchasing power declines?

items.title: Lower liquidity
items.description: How would funds be raised if some assets became difficult to sell?

items.title: Lower primary income
items.description: Which obligations come under pressure if business or primary income falls?

items.title: Higher financial obligations
items.description: How much flexibility remains if essential costs or payments rise?

sections.closing: These scenarios are used to clarify important questions. Advanced stress testing or ongoing monitoring, if offered, is scoped separately.

sections.heading: From understanding the wealth structure to prioritising risks
sections.intro: The review begins with the issue and financial circumstances. Its scope is then defined around the need and complexity of the wealth structure.

items.title: Initial assessment
items.description: Clarify the decision, principal concerns and fit with DNH’s services.

items.title: Define the review scope
items.description: Agree subjects, required information and engagement boundaries.

items.title: Understand the financial structure
items.description: Review relationships between assets, obligations, liquidity and income.

items.title: Identify and prioritise risks
items.description: Clarify vulnerabilities, important dependencies and matters requiring attention.

items.title: Conclude and define the next step
items.description: Set review priorities and identify an appropriate path for the decision or further work.

sections.note: Periodic monitoring, protective implementation or advanced analysis falls within the engagement only when separately defined and agreed.

sections.heading: What becomes clearer after a risk assessment?
sections.intro: The value of the assessment lies in identifying vulnerabilities and decision priorities.

groups.label: SERVICE POSITION
groups.title: How this assessment differs
bullets: Private Wealth Strategy: alignment of assets, goals and the broader wealth path
Portfolio Intelligence: investment mix and shared portfolio risks
Risk Management: vulnerabilities affecting the whole wealth structure

sections.note: The service assesses and prioritises risk; it does not guarantee value preservation or eliminate risk. Trading and protective implementation are not part of the base assessment.

sections.heading: Do not wait for a crisis to understand wealth risk
sections.heading_highlight: do not wait for a crisis
paragraphs: If wealth is concentrated, financially dependent on a business, or exposed to liquidity and future-obligation concerns, an initial assessment can be a practical starting point.
Submitting the form does not mean automatic acceptance or delivery of a full specialist assessment.
sections.closing: You do not need to provide confidential documents or complete asset details at the initial stage.
